beats.narration_slice: How were such immense structures planned?
beats.visual: A vertical archaeological engraving of the Giza plateau with a pyramid shown as a measured architectural reconstruction: faint charcoal baseline, corner sightlines, proportional guide marks, and a few scale figures beside limestone courses, all on sun-aged papyrus with restrained ochre and desert-blue accents.
beats.purpose: introduce the question of how a massive pyramid could be planned and laid out with precision
beats.continuity: first body image establishes the archaeological sketchbook world after the Egypt book transition

beats.narration_slice: How were heavy materials moved into place?
beats.visual: Engraved workers hauling a large limestone block on a wooden sledge across prepared ground, ropes visibly under tension; a faint alternative ramp contour appears as a lightly drawn hypothetical reconstruction rather than a definitive scene.
beats.purpose: show the physical problem of transporting heavy stone while keeping disputed transport methods visibly hypothetical
beats.continuity: moves closer from the overall pyramid plan to one construction task at ground level

beats.narration_slice: How did builders keep each side aligned?
beats.visual: Top-down oblique engraving of a pyramid foundation corner with taut surveying cords, straight reference lines, simple wooden measuring implements, and carefully squared limestone edges casting sparse dusty shadows.
beats.purpose: visualize the challenge of maintaining straight, accurately aligned pyramid sides
beats.continuity: shifts from moving blocks to the precision required when placing them

beats.narration_slice: What tools made the work possible?
beats.visual: A simple archaeological still life on papyrus: copper-era chisels, stone pounders, wooden mallets, rope, a wooden lever, and a plumb-like surveying implement arranged beside a partially worked limestone block, rendered as evidence objects rather than a labeled museum display.
beats.purpose: show historically plausible categories of tools associated with quarrying, shaping, moving, and measuring stone
beats.continuity: cuts from surveying in use to a close study of the physical implements themselves

beats.narration_slice: How was a project this complex organized?
beats.visual: Wide engraved scene linking quarry edge, hauling route, work crews, food preparation area, and worker settlement near the plateau through natural spatial flow; small groups perform different tasks without any modern hierarchy chart or readable labels.
beats.purpose: show that pyramid construction required coordinated labor, supply, logistics, and specialized work
beats.continuity: widens from individual tools to the larger human system needed to sustain construction

beats.narration_slice: What did the pyramids mean to the people who lived around them?
beats.visual: Quiet archival-style engraving of a completed pyramid dominating the desert horizon while nearby settlement figures, procession-like silhouettes, and cultivated land occupy the foreground; symbolic elements remain restrained and non-specific rather than inventing religious claims.
beats.purpose: raise the social and symbolic meaning of the pyramids without asserting a single interpretation
beats.continuity: moves from how the project functioned to how the finished monument related to surrounding life

beats.narration_slice: Which clues are solid evidence, and which interpretations remain debated?
beats.visual: A single archaeological composition with excavated limestone courses, tool marks, a sledge fragment, settlement remains, and surveying traces rendered in firm dark engraving, while possible ramp and organizational reconstructions appear only as pale, incomplete charcoal overlays fading into the papyrus.
beats.purpose: visually distinguish material archaeological evidence from more tentative reconstruction and interpretation
beats.continuity: turns the preceding historical questions into an explicit evidence-versus-hypothesis distinction

beats.narration_slice: That distinction matters, because this brief includes no source notes to check.
beats.visual: Close archaeological desk-like composition without readable writing: a few evidence fragments and measured drawings sit sharply rendered at the center, while empty papyrus margins and unfinished annotation strokes surround them, emphasizing the absence of supporting source material.
beats.purpose: show that the episode lacks source notes needed to verify detailed claims
beats.continuity: narrows from the broad evidence comparison to the specific limitation of this episode's source material

beats.narration_slice: So rather than turn uncertainty into a confident story, we stop where the evidence stops.
beats.visual: A partially reconstructed pyramid drawing ends deliberately at a crisp boundary: confirmed masonry and excavated traces are rendered in complete engraved lines on one side, while the unverified continuation dissolves into blank papyrus with only a few faint unfinished guide strokes.
beats.purpose: communicate the editorial decision to stop making claims once reliable evidence runs out
beats.continuity: resolves the evidence theme by transforming uncertainty into a deliberate visual stopping point suitable for the closing book echo
